study type: N/A (Describes a study involving sample collection and analysis, but doesn't specify a study type)
exposure: Bacterial infection in amniotic fluid and vaginal swabs
outcome: Presence of bacteria in vaginal swabs and amniotic fluid
Histological changes in amniotic sac tissue
cohort: 100 pregnant women at Hilla Teaching Hospital (50 having normal births and 50 having cesarean sections).
finding: Bacterial infection, particularly with E. coli, P. aeruginosa, and other identified species, was prevalent in both vaginal swabs and amniotic fluid, and was associated with histological changes in the amniotic sac, including lymphocyte infiltration, hemorrhage, and epithelial cell elongation.
mod_finding: Histological changes in the amniotic sac due to bacterial infection were observed in both women who had normal births and those who underwent cesarean sections.
